Specification of Communication Management AUTOSAR AP R25-11 [SWS_CM_00140] Minimum Send Interval monitoring for transmission requests for Triggers ⌈ To protect receivers from flooding/overload, each trigger shall have a configurable Minimum Send Interval (see ServiceInterfaceDeploymentEle- ment . minimumSendInterval ), which specifies the minimum amount of time that shall pass between two consecutive transmissions, i.e., the Minimum Send Interval limits the maximum Tx frequency of a given trigger in the network. If the application requests transmission of a trigger by calling Trigger::Send()/Send() , ara::com shall check, whether the time since the last successful handover of the trigger to the underlying transmission layer is greater than the specified Minimum Send Interval, i.e., the Minimum Send Interval is not violated. If the trigger has never been sent before, this shall also successfully pass the Minimum Send Interval check. If the Minimum Send Interval is not violated, ara::com shall process the transmission request by handing over the trigger to the transmission layer. The time of handover shall count as start of the new Minimum Send Interval monitoring. If the Minimum Send Interval is vio- lated, ara::com shall discard the transmission request and return error ComErrc:: kMinimumSendIntervalViolationError (see [SWS_CM_10432]). If the config- ured Minimum Send Interval ( ServiceInterfaceDeploymentElement . minimum- SendInterval ) of a trigger has the value 0, the Minimum Send Interval monitoring shall not be active for the corresponding trigger. ⌋ [SWS_CM_00142] Default value of Minimum Send Interval and disabling Mini- mum Send Interval monitoring for Triggers ⌈ If the configured Minimum Send Inter- val ( ServiceInterfaceDeploymentElement . minimumSendInterval ) of a trig- ger has the value 0, the Minimum Send Interval monitoring shall not be active for the corresponding trigger, i.e., ara::com will not limit the Tx frequency by dropping trans- mission requests. For each Trigger of a ServiceInterfaceDeployment (or the associated Event), 0 shall be the default value for the corresponding ServiceInter- faceDeploymentElement . minimumSendInterval . This means that unless Ser- viceInterfaceDeploymentElement . minimumSendInterval for a given event is explicitly configured to be > 0, the Tx rate is not limited by ara::com . ⌋ 7.5.17 Service trigger subscription For the service trigger subscription C++ API reference, see chapter 8.3.7.1.3.
